overview: The Xia is the first dynasty in Chinese tradition, associated by most Chinese scholars with the Erlitou archaeological culture of the middle Yellow River valley. Whether it was a historical state or a later political myth remains debated outside China, but the material culture of the period shows the first large-scale bronze production and palace architecture in the region.

items.text: Erlitou produces the earliest Chinese bronze ritual vessels using section-mold casting.
Irrigation canals and flood control works attributed to the legendary founder Yu the Great.
Bronze wine vessels with animal masks and jade ceremonial objects establish the forms that later dynasties copied.
Turquoise-inlaid bronze plaques with animal designs from Erlitou tombs.
Ancestor worship and divination practices appear in the archaeological record, anticipating Shang and Zhou religion.
The legend of Yu controlling the floods established the model of the virtuous ruler who brings order from chaos.
Millet farming and pig husbandry supported growing populations in the Yellow River valley.
Rammed-earth walls surrounded palace and temple complexes at Erlitou.
The concept of dynastic succession begins with the Xia, as Shang claims to have replaced it by Heaven's mandate.
The name Xia later became synonymous with Chinese civilization itself.

fall.text: According to tradition, the tyrant Jie was defeated by Tang of Shang at the Battle of Mingtiao.
